b: The **FAQ** on the home screen is up to date: how sync works and what the cloud icon's colours mean, what happens when two devices change at once, and a new answer on seeing which devices sync with your account.
The FAQ, the Coming soon list and the descriptions of Review, Practice and Exam are now part of the app itself, so they open offline too.
Review's description now counts seven card types, including Label cards.

After Study Suite updates, a short **What's new** panel slides up from the bottom of the home screen. If you've missed a few updates, the newest is written out and the earlier ones are listed by name: tap one to read it.
It shows once. Close it with **Got it** or the ×. If you're signed in, it won't show again on your other devices either.
Tap the version number at the bottom of the home screen to see every update, any time.
When a new version is ready, the Update button shows its name for a few seconds.
The Coming soon list is up to date: weak-spot practice arrived as **Gaps** in v0.11.0.
The **Pharmacology Index** is now added for everyone automatically, once. If you remove it, it stays removed.
**The Brain** atlas now comes along with the neuro weeks: when a week that links into the atlas is in your library and switched on, the atlas is added too. Removing the atlas keeps it removed.
Atlas links in a guide now open the atlas they belong to, ready for more atlases later.
The Brain atlas now sits under **Reference › Atlases** in Study packs and Your library, beside the Pharmacology Index. It used to be under Year 2 › CPC 3.
Reference is always listed last, below your year packs. In Topic guides, the atlas's reading guides stay where they were, after your week guides.
Pharmacology now takes its drug class names from the Pharmacology Index, so every class heading shows its proper name (for example "Selective COX-2 inhibitor (coxib)" instead of "Cox2 Inhibitor").
Without the index, Pharmacology shows the class names it had before.
New **Pharmacology Index** in Study packs: one summary per drug, written once from all the weeks that teach it. Add it to your library, or tap **+ Add** at the top of Pharmacology.

With it, each drug in Pharmacology shows its **core** facts first (mechanism, cautions, adverse effects, monitoring, interactions), then **Taught in**: each switched-on week that covers the drug, what it's used for there, and a link to that week's guide.
Pharmacology still only lists drugs from the packs you have switched on. The index fills in their summaries; it never adds drugs on its own.
The Pharmacology Index and The Brain atlas now say, under their names in Study packs and in your library, what you get by adding them.
Fixed: a few drug entries showed codes like "<" instead of "<".

Tap the bookmark icon at the top of a topic guide to bookmark it. Bookmarked guides are marked in the guide list and listed at the top of the Flagged page, where you can open them or remove the bookmark.
The Flagged link on Home now also shows how many guides you've bookmarked.
Bookmarks sync across your devices, like flags.

If a pack from your account couldn't download on this device (for example, it was published moments ago or you were offline), it now shows in Your library in its usual place, greyed out and marked "waiting to download", with a **Tap to retry** button. Before, you only saw a brief message.

New **Gaps** page: your topics ranked worst first, from the questions you got wrong last time and the cards you keep forgetting. Questions and cards you haven't tried yet don't count against you; they show as "not tried".
A topic is ranked once you've tried 5 of its items, or a third of them for small topics. Until then it waits under "Not enough answers yet".
See it week by week, or as one list with the worst topics first.
One tap on a topic starts a **Practice** set on it (the ones you got wrong first, then the ones you haven't tried) or a **Review** of its cards (the ones you forgot first).
Find Gaps on Home next to Flagged, in the Practice question map, on the Review screen and on the results page.
Review has a new **Cards marked Again** filter: study only the cards you last marked Again. It works with Flagged only too.
In the Brain atlas, turning Labels off now keeps the "Structures on this slice" list, so you can still pick a structure from it.
With Labels off, picking or tapping a structure shows just that one name: beside the drawing with its pointer on a wide screen, and on the structure itself on a phone.
The Reference button is now called Photo. It steps through Photo + drawing and Photo only.

The topic label above a question or card now stays hidden until you've answered, so it can't give the answer away. It appears when you submit (Practice), when you finish the exam (Exam), or when you tap Show answer (Review). Difficulty and the question number show as before.

notes.t: Figures work on iPhone and iPad
b: Interactive figures inside topic guides now respond on iPhone and iPad, in Safari and in the home-screen app. Before, they showed up but ignored taps. The "See it in the atlas" links inside guides work there too.
In Default packs, each course now lists its packs newest first: the latest week at the top (and the Brain atlas above the CPC 3 weeks), counting down to the first week of the course.

notes.t: Three planes up front, a bigger map
b: The 3D view now has its own button in the plane row of the Brain atlas, next to Axial, Coronal, Sagittal and Surface.
On a wide screen the little locator map sits large beside the drawing, with every level of the plane marked; tap a level line to go there. Narrow screens keep the thumbnail.
In the 3D view, a structure that goes by another name on another plane lights up there too (the cerebellum, the cerebral peduncle, the ventricle parts).
In the new 3D view, tapping a structure now lights it and names it as intended; v0.10.11 ignored the tap.

A new 3D button in the Brain atlas shows the axial, coronal and sagittal slices you are on as three glass panes intersecting in space, lined up so a structure meets itself from plane to plane. Drag to turn it, move any plane with its slider and watch it travel through the others, tap a structure to light it on every pane and read its name, or tap a pane's label to open that slice.

Tap a structure in the Brain atlas and the readout now ends with a "Read" link to the week guide section that teaches it, in Weeks 42–44. If that week's pack is not in your library the line names the guide without a link.

The Week 42–44 neuroanatomy guides can now hand you straight to the Brain atlas: a "See it in the atlas" line at the end of a section opens the matching slice or view, with the territories or a pathway already on where that helps. If the atlas pack is not in your library yet, the line offers to add it with one tap and then opens the view.

notes.t: Guides open the atlas where they point
b: A guide can now show the Brain atlas already set to the slice it is talking about, with the right switches on: the new atlas reading guides open at the mid pons, with a pathway lit, or with the reference scan up.

notes.t: Tap a structure, see its label
b: In the Brain atlas, tapping a structure (or picking one from the list, or revealing a quiz answer) now lights up its label as well: the name in the margin turns bold in the accent colour and its leader line follows, so you can see at once which label belongs to the shape you touched. Zoomed in, the name on the drawing lights the same way.
The highlighted structure itself is a little stronger, so it still stands out over a reference photo.

notes.t: The atlas map, pinch zoom, names at zoom
b: The little map beside each slice is now a proper locator: a side view from the head to the sacrum (so the cord levels have a place) or a view from above for the sagittal slices, with an eye and a shaded cone showing where you are looking from. Tap the map to open it large and tap any level line to jump there.
Pinch to zoom on phones and iPads, or hold ⌘ or Ctrl and scroll on a computer. Zoomed in, the names appear on the drawing itself.
Long names no longer run off the edge of the picture.
The phone layout now applies to the atlas cards in Review as well, and the surface and sagittal views show their orientation banner on every screen.
The Brain atlas now works on phones and iPads for everyone; no flag needed.
The structures on a slice are in a dropdown grouped by system (cortex, basal ganglia, brainstem, arteries…). Pick one to highlight it.
Buttons a slice cannot use are greyed out: Reference where there is no reference image yet, Territories where there is no arterial map, and each pathway where that slice has no drawing of it.

notes.t: The atlas as its own view, phone layout in beta
b: The Brain atlas now opens as its own full-width view, from Home and from the button under its poster in the guide. Back takes you to where you came from.
A "Structures on this slice" list sits under the picture: tap a name to highlight it, which is easier than hitting a small or overlapping structure with the mouse or a finger.

On phones and iPads the atlas is in early testing: the picture fills the width, the names are tappable chips, the orientation reads as text, and the extra tools sit behind More. To try it on your device, open studysuite.app/#beta once; studysuite.app/#nobeta turns it back off. Without the flag you still see the short notice.

notes.t: Atlas on desktop, guides in order
b: The Brain atlas is desktop-only for now: on phones and iPads the guide shows a short notice instead of the widget.
In the atlas, a structure's slices cycle both ways (Prev and Next) and show which one you are on.
Topic Guides stay in week order, so Previous and Next walk the course in sequence; the library keeps newest first.
The little map in the atlas now stays on the sagittal and surface views, with a beacon showing where you are.
Searching the atlas lists every slice a structure appears on; tap one to go straight there.
The library and the default packs now list the newest week first, so the current course sits at the top.
The Brain atlas sits above the Neuro weeks without showing a week number.

**A new kind of figure: the atlas.** A pack can carry a whole atlas — planes, levels, a shared list of structures — and the app draws it: pick Axial, Coronal, Sagittal or Surface, move through the levels, tap any structure to name it, search for one and jump to every slice that shows it, switch the labels off and Quiz yourself, add the arterial territories or a pathway, flip between the radiological and anatomical conventions, zoom in and drag, or show the real slice under the drawing.
Cards can open the atlas at a given level, and guides can link straight to a level.
First atlas pack: **The Brain — Neuro atlas**, coming in the next pack update.

**Figures you can work with.** Topic guides and cards can now carry interactive figures, not just pictures: scroll through levels, switch layers and views on and off, tap structures to name them, and find a lesion from its deficits. Each one has a Quiz me mode.
**New kinds of cards.** Some cards ask you to tap the answer on a figure; others show a figure and ask what it is or what it causes.
**Neuro I goes first.** Week 44 is the first pack to use them. On an older version of the app you'll see a still picture instead.

**Filter the question map.** In practice and exam sessions, a Filter menu on the question map lets you show only the questions you want: unanswered, answered, flagged, incorrect or correct. The map updates as you go. Hidden questions keep their numbers, and "Show all" brings everything back.
**Next and Previous follow the filter.** With a filter on, Next and Previous step through just the matching questions.
**No peeking in exams.** In exam mode the Correct and Incorrect options stay greyed out until you submit. Filters reset when you start a new session.

notes.t: Packs catch up with the app
b: **Packs catch up with the app.** If a pack was downloaded before your app knew about a new kind of card (for example the Label cards in Neuro I), the app now reads it again by itself, so nothing is missing. Your progress is kept.
**Clearer sources label.** In your library, a pack with every source switched on now says "All sources" instead of just "Sources", so it's clear nothing is filtered out.
**Pictures in questions and cards.** Some questions and cards now include an image, such as a scan or a diagram. It fits the screen on phones and computers.

**New card type: Label.** A figure with its labels covered by numbered boxes. Name each one, tap a box to check that label, or tap **Show answer** to uncover them all and see the full list. Then rate yourself as usual.
**Topic Guides search stays in reach.** The search box at the top of the topic list stays visible while you scroll the list.

**Clearing a search keeps your place.** In Topic Guides and Pharmacology, clearing a search brings back the full list without jumping to the top. The guide or drug you were on stays where it was on screen. In Pharmacology, the search box now also stays visible as you scroll.
Label cards need this version. Older versions of the app skip them, and everything else in a pack still works.

notes.t: Flag anything to come back to
b: **Flag anything to come back to.** A ⚑ Flag button on every question (Practice and Exam) and every card (Review). A flag stays until you clear it, whether you got the item right or wrong, and it follows you to your other devices.

**Practise just what you need.** Practice and Exam setup have two new filters: **Flagged** and **Incorrect** (questions you got wrong the last time you answered them). Tick both to get either. Review has **Flagged only**, which brings back every flagged card, due or not.
**A Flagged list.** "⚑ Flagged" on the home screen shows everything you've flagged, by week, with a link to each item's guide. Clear one flag, a whole week's, or all of them.

notes.t: Topic Guides open at the top again
b: **Topic Guides open at the top again.** The viewer still opens the last guide you were reading, but at its start, without jumping to your old spot or showing a "Back where you left off" message.
The topic list still opens at the guide you're reading.

notes.t: Topic Guides open where you left off, every time
b: **Topic Guides open where you left off, every time.** Coming back to the guides now reliably returns you to your spot, and **Start from the top** takes you to the top and stays there.
**The topic list opens at the guide you're reading.** With several weeks loaded, opening the list no longer drops you back at the start of the first week; it opens with your current guide in view.

notes.t: Pack updates follow to your other devices again
b: **Pack updates follow to your other devices again.** When you update a pack on one device, your other devices are meant to pick it up on their next sync. A device that had been open in the background could miss it and ask you to update again by hand; it now catches up on its own. Sync activity also shows which version of each pack a device has, and notes when an update was picked up from another device.

notes.t: Saving a guide on iPhone and iPad
b: **Saving a guide on iPhone and iPad.** In the Study Suite app on your iPhone or iPad Home Screen, the download button now opens the guide in a Safari window instead of doing nothing. Tap Share, then Print, to print it or save it as a PDF; tap the X to go back. On a computer, and in the browser on any device, the button works as before.

notes.t: Topic Guides pick up where you left off
b: **Topic Guides pick up where you left off.** Open guides and you're back in the guide and section you were last reading — on this device or another one signed in to the same account (close your laptop, open your iPad). A note says where you are, with a button to go back to the top of that guide, and the Topic Guides card on the home screen shows what you'll continue. If that guide isn't available any more — its pack is turned off or its source is switched off — guides open from the beginning as before, and your place comes back when you turn it on again. Text size and Fit width are now remembered on each device.

**Notices match your theme.** Pop-up notices are now cards in your theme's own colours — light on the light themes, dark on the dark and black themes — instead of a bright white box on dark pages and a dark box on light ones. On phones, longer notices now use the full width of the screen instead of wrapping into a narrow column.

notes.t: Previous and Next in Topic Guides
b: **Previous and Next in Topic Guides.** Under each guide there are now Previous and Next buttons, so you can move through a week's guides without opening the topic list. On a computer each button shows the title of the guide it leads to, and page numbers in the middle let you jump straight to any guide in that week. At the end of a week, Next carries on into the next week's first guide. On phones the buttons are compact, with a "9 / 25" counter between them, and the Fit button at the top is shorter so everything fits on screen. The Print button is now Download (just an arrow on phones) — it still prints the guide or saves it as a PDF.

notes.t: A note with each pack update
b: **A note with each pack update.** When a pack is updated, the "what's new" card on the home screen can now include a short note explaining what changed and why — for example, that a week's pack now includes what was taught at its CBL session. In Your library, the first sentence of the note shows beside a waiting update, and again after updating while the what's-new is showing; on a computer, hover over the row to read the whole note. Packs updated without a note look exactly as before.

notes.t: Tidier Sources panel for older packs
b: **Tidier Sources panel for older packs.** Packs that only have an Extras switch (such as the MSK weeks) no longer show an "All on" button or the note about sources, since there is nothing else to switch.

**Extras, kept but off.** A pack can now carry an "Extras" set: lower-yield questions and cards that repeat a question. They stay in the pack but are switched off by default, so they don't show up in Review, Practice or Exam, and they don't count in your totals. If you want them, open the pack's **Sources** in your library and turn on Extras for that pack; they then count like everything else. "All on" leaves Extras as you set it. When a pack update moves items into Extras, the update note in your library says so.

notes.t: Pack updates show in the header
b: **Pack updates show in the header.** When newer versions of your packs are published, the header button now shows a badge with the count: a tinted "Packs" button when only packs are waiting, or the usual lit "Update" button with the badge when a new version of Study Suite is out as well. Tapping the tinted button takes you to your library, where you accept pack updates per pack or all at once, exactly as before; nothing is applied from the header. Hover the button on a computer for the details. On phones the button briefly shows its label when something new is waiting.

notes.t: The Update button says its name
b: **The Update button says its name.** On phones the header buttons are icons, so a waiting update was only a lit arrow. Now, when an update is ready, the button briefly shows "Update" beside the arrow when you open the app, then settles back to the arrow. It also sits at the left of the header buttons, so nothing else shifts while it does. Nothing else changes.

**New packs reach every device.** When you add a study pack on one device, your other devices used to need a restart before they could download it if they had been open a while — the pack showed as "couldn't be downloaded yet" and stayed that way. Now a device re-reads the list of published packs the moment it meets a pack it doesn't know, and it also checks the list every few minutes while open, so new packs and pack updates appear on their own. Small wording fix: an offloaded pack's row in the library now says "offloaded", matching its button.

notes.t: Pack updates are yours to accept
b: **Pack updates are yours to accept.** The header **Update** button now lights up only for a new version of Study Suite itself. When a newer study pack is published, the library still shows what's new and offers the update — tap **↑ Update** there (or **Update all**) when you're ready. Once you accept it on one device, your other devices pick it up on their next sync as before. Previously the header button applied waiting pack updates too, so a tap meant as a refresh could update a pack you hadn't looked at yet.

**Choose your sources.** Packs can now say which course materials each question, card and guide came from — a lecture, a case, a module, a quiz. In your library, a pack that carries this shows a **Sources** button under its counts: open it and switch any source off to set its material aside everywhere (Review, Practice, Exam, the topic guides and Pharmacology). An item is hidden only when every source it draws on is off, so the counts show what's left. Guides that mix sources hide just the sections that are off, with a note at the top. Your switches sync to your other devices with your account. Week 42 · Psych III is the first pack with sources; the other Psych weeks follow.
**See where an item came from.** Under the guide link on every question and card, small tags name its sources. Tap one for the full name.
**A whole week in one tap.** In the topic pickers (Review, and the Practice and Exam setup screens), each week's heading now has an **All / None** button.
**Pack updates read better.** When a guide in an updated pack is renumbered, the what's-new note counts it as updated rather than removed and added.
**Authoring guide v2.22:** how a pack declares its sources and tags its items, guides, guide sections and drugs with them, with validator checks.

**Fix: Pharmacology fits on phones.** On an iPhone, some drug cards ran off the edge of the screen with oversized text, and the whole page shrank. The small source tags on each line now wrap inside the card, so every card fits the screen.
**Authoring guide v2.21:** a drug's source topic should be one short topic name, not a list of every topic it came from. The guide's validator now flags long ones.

notes.t: Sync activity from all your devices
b: **Sync activity from all your devices.** **Sync activity** in the account menu can now show any of your devices, not just the one you're on. Pick a device from the list to see what sync did there. Each device shares its activity, encrypted like the rest of your study data, the next time it syncs a change.
**Copy for troubleshooting** copies every device's activity as plain text, ready to paste if you're reporting a sync problem.
**Force sync** (a small link under the list) shares this device's activity straight away, even if nothing has changed.
Each device now keeps its last 100 sync events, up from 60.

notes.t: Fix: "Request an access code" works again
b: **Fix: "Request an access code" works again.** The link on the welcome screen now opens an email to request a code, as it used to. And the **Download the instruction set** link for making your own packs now shows for everyone, with or without an access code.

**A clearer home screen.** Your library now has its own panel, and the study packs for your course sit right below it — titled for your school (for example, **UofT Med Study Packs**), with how many you've added so far. Starting fresh? The home screen tells you where to begin.
**Fix:** every pack shows up after updating — a device that updated from an older version could leave some packs out of the library until you reloaded it.
**Fix:** packs waiting to download now show their real number of questions and cards.

**Smoother first sync after updating.** A device that had just updated could briefly say some packs "couldn't be downloaded" before sorting itself out. It now unlocks and downloads them straight away.

notes.t: Your study packs are now protected
b: **Your study packs are now protected.** The shared study packs are now encrypted, so only an access code can unlock them. If Study Suite asks, enter your access code once — with an account, that unlocks them on all your devices. Your packs, progress and settings stay exactly as they are.

**Lighter on your devices.** Packs you've switched off no longer need to take up space. On a new device, only the packs you have switched on are downloaded — the others still show in your library, greyed out, with a download button that brings them back (and switches them on) in one tap. Packs that have been off for a week are offloaded automatically (you can turn that off in **Settings → Storage**), or tap **Offload** under a pack's switch to do it now. Your progress is always kept, and your own custom packs are never offloaded.

**Tidier topic pickers.** With several packs active, the topic lists on the Review, Practice and Exam screens fold each pack's topics under its name, with a count of how many you've picked. Open only the pack you want.

**What's new in pack updates.** When a pack update is waiting, your library shows what it brings — for example "+24 questions · +49 cards · 4 new guides, 5 updated". After you update, a short note on the home screen sums up what changed. It shows once and goes away (or tap ✕).

notes.t: See which version of each pack you have
b: **See which version of each pack you have.** Your library now shows each pack's version next to its questions, cards and guides.

notes.t: Fix: pack updates now carry over reliably
b: **Fix: pack updates now carry over reliably.** If a pack had been switched on or off on another device, sync could keep that device's older version of the pack instead of the one you'd just updated to. The newest version you've accepted now always wins, and your other devices bring themselves up to it.

**One tap updates everything.** The **Update** button now brings in the new version of Study Suite *and* any updated study packs in one go. And once you update a pack on one device, your other devices pick up the same update on their next sync — no need to tap Update on each one.

**Access codes, your way.** You can now add more than one access code — from the account menu (**Add an access code**), or from **Settings → Access codes** if you use Study Suite without an account. Each code unlocks the study packs shared with its group, and with an account they appear on all your devices. Default study packs now show only what your codes unlock.

**Small sync fix.** When a device with an older copy of a pack synced, the pack could lose its record of when it was last switched on or off, which sync uses to settle changes made on two devices at once. That record is now always kept.
**Update prompts that show up.** If a new version comes out while Study Suite is open, the **Update** button now appears within a few minutes — in a browser tab too, not just the installed app.
**Tidier account menu.** Sync activity and Your devices sit right under **Sync now**, and the security options are in a clearer order.

notes.t: Fix: packs could go missing when several were loaded
b: **Fix: packs could go missing when several were loaded.** On Safari and iPhone, the browser storage Study Suite used could run out of room with several packs loaded — the newest pack then wasn't saved, and sync could spread the gap to your other devices. Study Suite now keeps your data in the browser's larger storage (moved over automatically), tells you plainly if it ever can't save, and never lets a pack that's only missing from one device be removed from your account. If a pack disappeared, add it back once and it will stay.

**A clearer welcome.** New here? Sign in, or enter your access code — then choose to create an account (your code is filled in for you) or use Study Suite without one. Creating an account keeps your progress safe and synced across your devices.

**See your devices.** Account menu → **Your devices** lists every browser or installed app that syncs with your account, with the app version it's on and when it last synced. Give this device a name you'll recognise — names are saved inside your encrypted study data. **Sync activity** now shows which device each change came from and the app version on every entry, to make any sync question quick to sort out.

notes.t: More reliable pack switches across devices
b: **More reliable pack switches across devices.** Turning a pack on or off on one device now always carries over when another device synced in the meantime.

notes.t: Sync combines your devices instead of asking
b: **Sync combines your devices instead of asking.** If you study on your phone and your laptop between syncs, Study Suite now puts both together — cards, question history, past exams, packs and settings — instead of asking which copy to keep. If the same card was studied on both, the most recent review counts; answers to the same question on both are all kept in your history.
**Keeps itself up to date.** While Study Suite is open it checks for changes from your other devices every few minutes, and it syncs as soon as you're back online.
**Sync status at a glance.** The cloud is green when you're in sync, yellow if the last sync is a few minutes old or you're offline, and red if something needs your attention.

**Pop-ups open in front again.** Some confirmation boxes could open behind the window you were in — for example **Sign out other devices** in the account menu, or **Clear history** in Settings — so it looked like nothing happened. They now always appear on top of whatever you opened them from.

notes.t: Sync fix: packs no longer switch off or disappear
b: **Sync fix: packs no longer switch off or disappear.** Having Study Suite open in two tabs or windows at once — or the installed app and a browser tab on the same computer — could let an older copy save over your newer changes, and sync then spread the older copy to your other devices. Now only one copy is active at a time: open Study Suite somewhere new and the other copy pauses, with a **Use it here** button to switch back. A paused copy never saves or syncs, so nothing gets overwritten.
**Sync activity** in the account menu shows what sync did recently on this device, in case anything ever looks off.

**Sign out other devices** (account menu → Security) signs your account out everywhere except the device you're on. Their study data stays on them; they just sign in again to keep syncing. To sign out everywhere at once, tick **Also sign out on all my other devices** when you sign out.

**A cleaner header.** The top bar now just says **Study Suite**, and its buttons — Home, Add to home / Refresh / Update, and your account — share one look. On phones they're icon-only, so nothing is crowded. **Skip** is now a small link under the answers, so the Previous / Submit / Next buttons fit on phones again.

**Up-to-date descriptions.** The home screen, FAQ and README now describe everything Study Suite does — including a new **Studying** section in the FAQ (how Practice orders questions, leaving and resuming exams, what topics are, the Pharmacology view) — and **Coming soon** shows what's planned next: weak-spot practice, easier pack-making, pasting a pack as text, flashcard import and a gentle first-run guide.
**Choose topics** in Review now lists a handful of real topics per week — Week 38 goes from over a hundred one-card topics to 14 — grouped by week, and each week folds away.
**Practice and Exam setup** can be narrowed to the topics you pick, and exam weighting by topic now balances across those same topics.
The **Home** button shows a proper icon everywhere (some devices showed an empty box).
**Add to Home Screen** now explains the easy way to bring your progress along: sign in to your account inside the installed app. No account? Backup all and Restore backup still work.
On phones, Settings and the Add to Home Screen steps fit the screen — no more cut-off options.
The **Privacy Policy** and **Terms** pages now match the app, including your chosen theme.
**Tidier sync choice.** When your device and your account both have changes, each "Keep" button now sits right under the copy it keeps, so it's clear which is which.

notes.t: Practice and exams remember what you've done
b: **Practice and exams remember what you've done.**

**Question history.** Practice now puts questions you've never answered first and the ones you've seen at the end — the ones you got wrong last time ahead of the ones you got right. They're marked on the question map, and each has **View prior answer** so you can see what you picked before. Prefer only new ones? Turn on **Unanswered questions only**.
**Fresh exams.** Exams pick questions you haven't answered yet first, keeping your weighting — or choose **Fresh only** to never repeat, or **Any** for the old behaviour.
**Skip.** A new **Skip** button moves on without answering, so the question isn't counted as seen.

**Set up before you start.** Tapping Practice or Exam opens a short setup screen — difficulty, fresh questions, weighting and timer, all in one place and remembered for next time. The difficulty bar on the home screen and the exam options in Settings have moved here.
**Exams you can come back to.** Leave an exam part-way and it's saved, with the timer paused. Tap Exam to resume, or start fresh — the questions you'd answered are submitted first.
**Past exams.** Your last 20 exams, including partial ones, are listed on the Exam card with their scores. Tap **Review** to go through any of them again.
You can clear your question history in Settings — for everything, or for one pack.
**Clearer welcome screen** — tidier layout, plus wording that makes plain what signing in does and what using Study Suite without an account means. "Class code" is now "access code".
Question history, past exams and any exam in progress are included in **Backup all** and sync.

**Accounts and sync are here.** Create a free, optional account and your packs and progress follow you between your phone, laptop and tablet. It's end-to-end encrypted: your data is locked on your device before it's uploaded, so nobody else can read it — including me.
**A new welcome screen:** sign in, create an account, or keep using Study Suite without one. Tap the **?** to see what going without an account means.
**The account menu** (the person icon, top right) shows your sync status and has **Sync now**, plus security settings: change password, new recovery code, change email, and delete account.
**Keep your recovery code safe.** If you forget your password, it's the only way back into your synced data. Your studying on your own devices is never at risk.
**You're always asked.** If two devices change at the same time, you see both copies and choose which to keep — nothing is overwritten behind your back.
**Free during the beta.** Creating an account needs your class code during early access.
The app now has a **Privacy Policy** and **Terms**, linked at the bottom of the page.
Everything still works without an account, exactly as before.
**Small polish.** A few visual touch-ups behind the scenes. Nothing changes in how you study.

notes.t: Your study day now follows your clock
b: **Your study day now follows your clock.** The daily limit on new cards used to reset at midnight UTC — 8 pm in Toronto. It now resets at your own local midnight, and it follows you if you travel. Crossing time zones never hands you a second day's worth of new cards.
Typing in a text box no longer triggers the review and quiz keyboard shortcuts.
Some behind-the-scenes groundwork for features coming later.

notes.t: Practice picks up where you left off
b: **Practice picks up where you left off.** Leaving Practice part-way — to check a guide, take a break, or close the tab — used to throw away every answer. Now your session is kept: the question order, what you picked, what you've submitted and how long each one took. Open Practice again and you're asked to **Resume** (it tells you how many you've submitted) or **Start fresh**. The Practice card on the home screen shows when a session is waiting.
Resuming after you've changed which packs are loaded simply skips any questions that are no longer there, and tells you how many.
**Finish & summary** or **Start fresh** clears the saved session, as you'd expect.
The saved session is included in **Backup all** / **Restore backup**.
Exams are unchanged: still timed, still one sitting.

**Small fixes & polish.** The Topic Guides search icon is now easier to tap and plays nicer with screen readers, and tapping it highlights your previous search so you can type straight over it. Plus a handful of small under-the-hood sturdiness fixes.

**Quicker search in Topic Guides.** There's now a little search icon next to the "Topic Guides" title. Tap it to open the topic list and jump straight into the search box — no extra clicks to start looking.

**Pharmacology search, refined.** The search box now lives **permanently at the top** of the Pharmacology view (with a little search icon). As you type, matches **light up inside the entries** and a **results list slides in** so you can jump straight to a drug, class, or side effect — clear the box and it tucks away on its own. A touch of spacing polish in the header, too.

notes.t: Pharmacology view — easier to get around
b: **Pharmacology view — easier to get around.** The drug index now has a navigable **sidebar**: tap the **Pharmacology** heading to open a list of every drug by class, and tap any drug to jump straight to it. Searching now **highlights your matches** right inside each entry and shows a quick results list in the sidebar — so finding a specific drug, class, or side effect is much faster.

**New: a Pharmacology view.** Study Suite now builds a cross-week **drug index** from the packs you have turned on. When your active packs include drug data, a **Pharmacology** panel appears on the home screen — open it for one consolidated entry per medication, organized by drug class, with the use, mechanism, dosing, cautions, adverse effects, monitoring, and interactions gathered in one place.

**It builds itself from your library.** The same drug mentioned across several weeks is merged into a single growing entry — turn more packs on and it fills in; turn packs off and it shrinks, just like the Topic Guides list.
**Every fact links back to its source.** Each line carries a chip showing the week and topic it came from; tap it to jump straight to that week's guide.
**Search** drugs, classes, or effects to filter instantly.
Your existing packs gain this automatically as they're updated — packs without drug data simply don't contribute, so nothing else changes.
**Tidy-up.** Small formatting polish to the prefilled access-code request email (cleaner subject line).

**Easier access-code requests.** The Request an access code button now opens an email that's already filled in with a short template (name, school/occupation, how you heard about Study Suite) — just fill the blanks and send.

notes.t: Copy a pack error in one tap
b: **Copy a pack error in one tap.** The "pack won't load" message now has a **Close and Copy** button — it copies the full error (which file, which item, and a link to the authoring guide) to your clipboard and closes, so you can paste it straight to your assistant to fix the pack.
**Request an access code.** The early-access screen now has a **Request an access code** button that opens a pre-addressed email, so you can ask for one without hunting for a contact.

notes.t: Clearer errors when a pack won't load
b: **Clearer errors when a pack won't load.** If you drop in a pack that has a problem — invalid JSON, or a question/card that's missing something — the app now tells you instead of quietly doing nothing. The message points to where the issue is (the file, or which item) so you or your assistant can fix the source pack.

**Smarter shuffle.** A small follow-up to the shuffled answers: choices like "All of the above" or "None of the above" now stay in place while the other options shuffle around them, so they always read correctly.

**Answers now shuffle.** In Practice, Exam, and Review, the answer options are now mixed up each time, so the correct choice isn't always in the same spot. Nothing you need to do — it works with every pack you already have, and your scores and progress are unaffected.

**A peek at what's next.** Added a new item to the **Coming soon** list: a **Pharmacology guide** — a cross-week drug index that builds itself from the packs you have turned on, gathering each medication's uses, mechanism, cautions, and side effects in one place, with links back to every week and topic it appears in. (Not live yet — just on the roadmap.)

**Access codes, smoother.** Behind the scenes, access codes are now checked against a small published list that updates on its own — so a newly shared code works right away, without waiting for an app update.

**Early access begins.** Study Suite now asks for an **access code** the first time you open it. If you don't have one yet, there's a button on that screen to request one. Already unlocked on another device? Use **Restore backup** right from the lock screen and you're back in. (Your code only needs to be entered once per device.)

**Topic Guides on mobile.** The guide reader is much nicer on a phone now: the guide fills the full width of the screen, the **Back** button tucks into a back arrow, and the zoom and Fit / Save buttons sit in a tidy stack in the corner instead of spilling off the edge.
**Footer fix.** The footer goes back to its original single line on desktop, with the tidy stacked rows kept just for mobile.

notes.t: Easier to grab the instruction set
b: **Easier to grab the instruction set.** The "instruction set" mentioned in the FAQ (and the README) is now a direct download link to the authoring guide.
**Tidier footer.** The footer attribution is now laid out in clean rows instead of one long line — nicer on mobile.

**Installed-app updates.** When you run Study Suite as an installed app (added to your home screen), the header now shows a **Refresh** button instead of "Add to home" — and it turns into **↑ Update** when a newer app or pack is available, so you can update with one tap instead of quitting and reopening. The "Add to home" button is also tidier now.

**Pack updates.** When a default pack you've added gets a newer version, the app now flags it — an **Update** button appears on that pack in your Content library (and an **Update all**), so you no longer have to remove and re-add it. Updating keeps your review progress.
**Tidier library order.** Packs in your Content library now sort by week within each course (matching the Default study packs), instead of the order you added them.

**Topic Guides in order.** The Topic Guides side panel now lists your packs in curriculum order (by school, year, and week) instead of the order you happened to add them — matching how your library is organized.

**Dark-mode contrast fixes.** Several controls were hard to read in Dark and Black modes — the "Add to library" buttons (which also flipped to a harsh white on hover), the answer tiles in ordering questions, unselected topic chips in Review, and the dropdowns in matching questions. All now have clear, theme-matched styling, and native menus/scrollbars follow the dark theme too.

notes.t: Follow the badge to what's new
b: **Follow the badge to what's new.** When you open the Default study packs, the "new" badge now follows the hierarchy down — flagging the school, year, and course that contain new packs, and tagging the new pack itself — so you can see exactly what was added. A pack stops being flagged once you've drilled down far enough to actually see it.

**A calmer home screen.** The Default study packs section now collapses once you've added content (it stays open while your library is empty). When the author publishes new default packs, the section shows a small "N new" badge and pops open once to show you — after that it just keeps the badge until you open it. Opening it clears the badge.

**Optional term/semester grouping.** Packs can now carry an optional term or semester that nests between year and course — in both your library and the Default study packs — for programs split into terms. Packs that don't use it look exactly the same as before.

**Library grouping fixed.** Your loaded packs now sit under their school, year, and course — matching the Default study packs layout — instead of all landing under "Other." Packs you already had repair themselves automatically.
**Sensible course order.** Courses now appear in their natural chronological order (e.g. ITM → CPC 1 → CPC 2) rather than alphabetically.
**Topic picker fixed.** In Review, "Select all" now highlights every topic and studies them all, and "Clear" deselects everything — the two buttons used to behave backwards.

**Your library is organized now.** The Content library is grouped the same way as the Default study packs — by school, then year and course — so a big library stays tidy. Whatever you've toggled on jumps to the top of its group, keeping what you're actively studying front and centre.
**A real app icon.** Study Suite now has its own logo — a navy stack of study cards — that shows in your browser tab and when you add the app to your home screen.

**Topic Guides match your theme.** Opening a topic guide in Dark or Black mode used to show a bright page — guides now follow whichever theme and mode you're in, recolor instantly when you switch, and do so reliably across all your packs.
**Theme polish.** Selected difficulty and school chips (and the settings toggles) now use the theme's accent color instead of black, so things look consistent in every theme.
**Get in touch.** The footer has a new row — **Support**, **Feedback**, and **Contact me** — each opens a pre-addressed email.

**Dark mode (and true black).** Study Suite now has **Light, Dark, and Black (OLED)** modes. By default it **follows your device** automatically — and you can pick whether "dark" means the regular Dark or the deeper Black. You can also force any mode in **Settings → Appearance**.
**Two color themes.** Choose between **Navy** (the new default) and **Warm** (the original paper-and-oxblood look) — each comes in all three modes.
**Nicer switches.** The on/off settings (and the pack toggles in your library) are now smooth sliding toggles.

notes.t: Study Suite has a new home: [studysuite.app](https://studysuite.app)
b: **Study Suite has a new home: [studysuite.app](https://studysuite.app).** That's the app's permanent address — bookmark it, and use it when adding the app to your home screen.

**Smoother prompts.** Confirmations — like removing a pack or leaving a session partway through — and little status messages now appear as clean in-app dialogs and toasts instead of the browser's own pop-up boxes. (Browsers start blocking those after a while, so this is more reliable too.)
**Quick changelog.** The version number in the footer is now a link straight to these release notes on GitHub.
**Cleaner Topic Guides navigation.** A few improvements to reading topic guides:

The topic list no longer covers the guide. Click the **Topic Guides** title at the top (note the little ▾) any time to slide open the searchable list; it tucks away again as soon as you pick a topic. It also starts closed now — so when you jump straight to a guide from a flashcard or a question explanation, you land right on the content, with nothing in the way.
The **← Back** button shows where it'll take you on a small second line — *to Practice*, *to Exam*, *to Review*, or *to Home* — so you always know where you'll land before tapping it.
**Now just "Study Suite."** The app's name is officially **Study Suite** — the browser tab, header, and home-screen icon all read that now.
**Wording tidy-up.** Freshened some of the language across the FAQ, the Coming soon list, and the install steps — same features, just clearer (and a little cheekier) phrasing.

notes.t: A heads-up about the road ahead
b: **A heads-up about the road ahead.** The "Coming soon" list now includes the plan to give Study Suite its own home: once it's out of beta, it'll move off its current address to **studysuite.app**. You'll get plenty of notice, and no data will be lost. (Accounts & sync and flashcard import are still on the list too.)

notes.t: A new FAQ, right on the home screen
b: **A new FAQ, right on the home screen.** Scroll to the bottom and you'll find two buttons — **Coming soon** and **FAQ**. The FAQ answers the questions people actually ask: is it really free, where your data lives and who can see it (no one but you), how to back up and move between devices, offline use, installing it like an app, and making your own packs. It also explains what's coming with accounts and sync — including how your data will be end‑to‑end encrypted so I can't read it, and how sync will work as an optional, affordable add‑on.
**Tidier footer.** The old "Features coming soon" list now tucks neatly behind the Coming soon button, so the home screen stays clean.

**Search inside your topic guides.** The Topic Guides search box now looks inside the guides themselves, not just the titles. Type a term and you'll see matching topics plus snippets showing where it comes up in the content — click a result to jump straight to that spot, with the word highlighted.

**Exams balance themselves.** Exams now split evenly across your active study packs automatically, and re-balance whenever you add or remove a pack — there's nothing to set up. You can still fine-tune the mix in Settings if you'd like.
Print / Save-as-PDF works again from the Topic Guides viewer.
The version number in the footer is now always accurate.
